raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+StatefulDataLoader+generator (related but different resume fixes: #4156, #7974, #7819)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

New CPU test `tests/trainer/test_sft_dataloader_resume_rng_on_cpu.py` (picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` via the `*_on_cpu.py` pattern). It calls the real `SFTTrainer._build_dataloader` with a stub engine and checks:

1. resume: after saving dataloader state + `torch.get_rng_state()`, rebuilding, restoring both and building the iterator, the next batches **and** subsequent global CPU RNG draws match the uninterrupted run;
2. building train/val iterators does not change `torch.get_rng_state()`;
3. generator seeds are distinct per dp rank and between train and val.

Locally (torch 2.15.0, torchdata 0.11.0):

```
with the fix:    3 passed
without the fix: 3 failed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `check_license.py` and `check_docstrings.py` pass on the touched files.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. The existing (previously unused by the SFT trainer) `trainer.seed` in `sft_trainer_engine.yaml` now seeds the dataloader generators.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/sft_trainer.py`: pass `generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + dp_rank)` to the train dataloader and `seed + dp_size + dp_rank` to the val dataloader, with `seed = config.trainer.seed`.
  - Per **dp** rank, not global rank: ranks in one dp group restore the same `data_{dp_rank}.pt`, so they must derive the same `base_seed`.
  - Separate train/val streams, so building a val iterator can never shift the train one.
  - Batch order is unchanged: `DistributedSampler` shuffles from its own `seed + epoch`; the generator only feeds the iterator's `base_seed` (worker seeding).
- `tests/special_sanity/check_license.py`: add the `Copyright 2026 Individual Contributor:` header (the 2025 variant already exists; other organizations already have `_26` variants) for the new test file.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (ruff, ruff-format, license, docstrings run on the touched files).
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed: no user-facing config or API change.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. The new `*_on_cpu.py` test runs in `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, update the submodule reference. Not applicable.

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+# Copyright 2026 Individual Contributor: Jinhong Lin
+#

+# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+# You may obtain a copy of the License at
+#

+# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+# limitations under the License.
+"""Resuming SFT from a checkpoint must not perturb the restored global CPU RNG.
+
+The checkpoint manager saves and restores ``torch.get_rng_state()``. Building the train
+dataloader iterator after that restore must not draw from the global CPU RNG, otherwise
+the resumed run continues from a different RNG state than an uninterrupted run.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import torch
+from omegaconf import OmegaConf
+
+from verl.trainer.sft_trainer import SFTTrainer
+
+
+def _build_trainer(dp_rank=0, dp_size=1):
+    config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "data": {"train_batch_size": 4 * dp_size, "pad_mode": "no_padding", "num_workers": 0},
+            "trainer": {"seed": 1},
+        }
+    )
+    engine = MagicMock()
+    engine.get_data_parallel_rank.return_value = dp_rank
+    engine.get_data_parallel_size.return_value = dp_size
+    trainer = SimpleNamespace(config=config, engine=engine, train_dataset=list(range(64)), val_dataset=list(range(32)))
+    SFTTrainer._build_dataloader(trainer)
+    # The collator is not under test; batches of ints keep the comparison simple.
+    trainer.train_dataloader.collate_fn = torch.utils.data.default_collate
+    trainer.val_dataloader.collate_fn = torch.utils.data.default_collate
+    return trainer
+
+
+def test_resume_preserves_batches_and_global_cpu_rng():
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    trainer = _build_trainer()
+    it = iter(trainer.train_dataloader)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        next(it)
+    dataloader_state, rng_state = trainer.train_dataloader.state_dict(), torch.get_rng_state()
+    expected_batches = [next(it).tolist() for _ in range(2)]
+    expected_draws = torch.rand(4)
+
+    # A fresh process: rebuild the dataloader, restore both states, then build the iterator.
+    torch.manual_seed(12345)
+    resumed = _build_trainer()
+    resumed.train_dataloader.load_state_dict(dataloader_state)
+    torch.set_rng_state(rng_state)
+    resumed_it = iter(resumed.train_dataloader)
+
+    assert [next(resumed_it).tolist() for _ in range(2)] == expected_batches
+    assert torch.equal(torch.rand(4), expected_draws)
+
+
+def test_building_iterators_does_not_consume_global_cpu_rng():
+    trainer = _build_trainer()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    before = torch.get_rng_state()
+    iter(trainer.train_dataloader)
+    iter(trainer.val_dataloader)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.get_rng_state(), before)
+
+
+def test_generators_are_seeded_per_dp_rank_and_split_train_from_val():
+    seeds = []
+    for dp_rank in range(2):
+        trainer = _build_trainer(dp_rank=dp_rank, dp_size=2)
+        seeds.append(trainer.train_dataloader.generator.initial_seed())
+        seeds.append(trainer.val_dataloader.generator.initial_seed())
+    assert len(set(seeds)) == len(seeds)

@@ -241,6 +241,12 @@ def _build_dataloader(self):
         self.train_batch_size_per_dp = self.global_batch_size // dp_size
         self.collate_fn = SFTTensorCollator(config.data.pad_mode)
 
+        # Without an explicit generator, every iterator construction draws its base seed from the
+        # global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpointed RNG state is
+        # restored, so training continues from a different RNG state than an uninterrupted run.
+        # Seed per dp rank (ranks in one dp group load the same data_{dp_rank}.pt) and keep the
+        # validation stream separate so building a val iterator never shifts the train one.
+        seed = config.trainer.seed
         self.train_dataloader = StatefulDataLoader(
             dataset=self.train_dataset,
             batch_size=self.train_batch_size_per_dp,
@@ -250,6 +256,7 @@ def _build_dataloader(self):
             pin_memory=False,
             drop_last=True,
             pin_memory_device=device_name,
+            generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + dp_rank),
         )
 
         if self.val_dataset:
@@ -265,6 +272,7 @@ def _build_dataloader(self):
                 pin_memory=False,
                 drop_last=True,
                 pin_memory_device=device_name,
+                generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + dp_size + dp_rank),
             )
         else:
             self.val_dataloader = None
